notes.note: Reading chosen: @nocase applies to the matching of the same regexp call; whether it affects later matchings is not tested.
Uses an inline AnyValue as inpar, which violates both readings (specific value only, or specific value/pattern) and the template (value) formal restriction.
Statically known value list as expression is rejected per the restriction; Titan does not implement this check (value list fulfils template (present)), hence the warning.
Literal error-cause reading; a value list passed through an unrestricted template parameter so the error is detected at runtime (ttcn3verdict:error).
Type mismatch is statically known, so reject is expected (as in the ETSI ATS for static error causes). Titan accepts it, following the older CR 6424 resolution; V4.17.1 lists it as an error.
Titan rejects substr on arrays; the standard explicitly allows arrays as inpar, so the warning is a Titan limitation.
Titan rejects substr on arrays (Titan limitation). The test only shows that the result is assignable to a record of; differing index ranges are not covered.
Present restriction of the result is not directly observable; the test assigns the result to a template (present) variable and checks the matching.
Value restriction is observed by assigning the result to a template (value) variable and checking isvalue/valueof.
First reading chosen; a statically known value-list element in a record of template is rejected.
